feed.title: The Embodied Neural Computation and Awareness Lab
feed.subtitle: Most cognitive neuroscience research, especially concerning humans, treats the brain as if it were a standalone computer. In reality, neural "computation" both influences and is itself modulated by biological processes elsewhere in the body. We study how the brain-body axis shapes our conscious experiences of the world and of ourselves. To this end, we integrate computational and empirical approaches to concretely link biological mechanisms with downstream psychological manifestations, leveraging a variety of behavioral (e.g., perceptual psychophyics) and non-invasive physiological (e.g., electroencephalography/EEG, cardiography, blood pressure) measures and interventions (e.g., electrical muscle stimulation, galvanic vestibular stimulation). Our lab space is located in the basement of the Skaggs Research Building, where we host a state-of-the-art EEG facility.
